root.name: Dutch Defense: Leningrad, Basman System
root.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. g3 c6 3. Bg2 g6 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. O-O Nh6

overview: Black plays the Leningrad set-up with ...c6 and ...Nh6, aiming for ...d6 and ...e5 or ...Qb6 pressure. White fianchettoes and can seek a central break or c5 and Nh6-attacking ideas. The Basman move order is a rare, flexible version of the main Leningrad.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bg2, Nf3, O-O and aim for e4 or c5 expansion
Play against the Nh6 with Bxh6 or Ne5

black_ideas.idea: Control e4 and attack on the kingside with ...f4

typical_structures.structure: Leningrad pawns f5, g6 with fianchetto

character.notes: The Dutch brings unbalanced play with both sides attacking.

structure.notes: Neither side has committed the centre.

approach.notes: Basman Variation is uncommon but the Leningrad is a standard choice.

level.notes: Plans are clear but the Dutch punishes weak moves.

sublines_that_differ.name: Main Leningrad
sublines_that_differ.how: Black castles before committing the knight; more common.
